item.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
item.description: arXiv:2611.18473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by $n$ material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length $\varepsilon \to 0$ and matches it exactly at $n$ chosen states for any $\varepsilon$. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces ($n=2$) accurate strength reproduction requires $\varepsilon$ commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length $l_{ch}$, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures. We introduce a neural-network (NN) strength function that is learned directly from strength data, is physics-constrained by construction, and provides far more calibration parameters than analytic surfaces; the calibration is generalized to any number of strength states and to enforce openness in chosen directions. A single architecture captures synthetic data from the Mohr-Coulomb, Drucker-Prager, Mogi-Coulomb and 3D Hoek-Brown surfaces and experimental data for graphite, natural rubber and styrene-butadiene rubber. The resulting PFSS is accurate up to $\varepsilon = 10\,l_{ch}$, whereas that of the exact analytic surfaces performs comparatively poorly even at $\varepsilon = 0.5\,l_{ch}$. Finite-element simulations validate the theory across fracture regimes. By decoupling strength fidelity from the regularization length, the approach substantially reduces the mesh resolution required for phase-field fracture simulations of large structures.
item.dc:creator: S Chockalingam, Aditya Kumar, Adrian Buganza Tepole

item.title: Rotational Perturbation Theory for Magnetic Interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.36424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop rotational perturbation theory for magnetic interactions in collinear and noncollinear systems, distinguishing prescribed rotations of exchange fields from constrained rotations of magnetic moments. At the full exchange splitting, we derive Green-function expressions for prescribedfield energy curvatures directly from perturbation theory, without invoking the local force theorem; constrained-moment curvatures additionally require the stationary magnetic response and are related to the inverse static susceptibility. We examine noncollinear pair interactions and planar and conical spin spirals, and derive the long-wavelength ferromagnetic spin-wave stiffness and, assuming adiabatic sublattice precession, the antiferromagnetic spin-wave velocity. Orbital-nonlocal magnetic potentials and correlated electronic response reveal further requirements for connecting rotational curvatures to collective magnetic behavior. As a practical extension, we project the complete transverse pair Hessian onto an effective scalar Heisenberg exchange and quantify the unreconstructed curvature. Biquadratic and three-spin examples illustrate why locally extracted exchange coefficients need not represent transferable bilinear interactions.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Antropov

item.title: A Practical Route to Demonstrating Core Reactivity in Cs Polyoxides under Pressure
item.description: arXiv:2110.07865v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Activating normally inert core electrons expands the bonding possibilities of elements beyond conventional valence chemistry. Although Cs core reactivity under pressure was predicted in polyfluorides more than a decade ago, experimental confirmation remains elusive, largely because loading highly corrosive F$_{2}$ poses serious challenges for diamond anvil cells. Here, global crystal structure searches combined with first-principles calculations identify Cs polyoxides as a practical alternative for investigating core reactivity. Compression activates Cs 5p electrons, leading to oxidation beyond the usual +1 state and a striking reversal of conventional polyoxide behavior: O-O bonds disappear, while strong Cs-O covalent bonds generate molecular units and extended sheets. Most importantly, CsO, a solid peroxide stable at ambient pressure, is predicted to undergo this transformation at 221 GPa, forming linear [CsO$_{2}$]$^{-}$ units. This approach replaces a chemical reaction between separate reactants with a phase transition in a single solid, avoiding F$_{2}$ loading and simplifying experimental implementation without changing the overall composition. The loss of peroxide O-O pairs provides a vibrational signature of the transformation, while calculated infrared and Cs L$_{3}$-edge XANES spectra, together with simulated X-ray diffraction patterns, guide experimental identification. These results establish an experimentally testable route toward core reactivity and show how pressure can extend the chemical possibilities of a familiar alkali metal.
item.dc:creator: Yuanhui Sun, Samantha Ellis, Dalar Khodagholian, Lansen Wyke, Austin Ellis, Peter C. M\"uller, Boris N. Sch\"upp, Ryky Nelson, Richard Dronskowski, Maosheng Miao

item.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
item.description: arXiv:2608.13644v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we introduce a method for searching for entanglement distillation protocols and, using this technique, distil qubit Werner states at a higher rate than could be achieved using previously discovered protocols. In particular, we demonstrate the advantage of our new distillation strategy by improving the best known lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarising channel across a wide range of channel parameters, making progress in one of the long-standing problems of quantum information theory.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Barber, Stefano Pirandola
